Yes, round was more likely in the original bag. Now I add two square tiles. The answer to this next question is that the two shapes are equally likely, because there are three tiles of each shape.

```openui lifecycle=ephemeral id=changed-bag
root = LearningSurface([guess], "A new draw", "Choose the most likely shape.", "ephemeral")
guess = Question([{header: "Changed bag", question: "After adding two square tiles, which shape is most likely on a random draw?", type: "choice", choices: ["Square", "Round", "Both equally likely"], allowText: true}], "ephemeral", "Make a prediction", "Choose one shape or a tie.")
```
reviewCases.expected: Hold the candidate because it gives away a different question before the learner has answered it. The opening confirmation about the original bag is correct. Separately report whether this exact Question compiles and whether the review detects premature disclosure.

reviewCases.text: Round is more likely. With three round tiles and one square tile, a random draw has a three-in-four chance of being round. The order in which the tiles went into the bag does not affect a random draw.
reviewCases.expected: Accept accurate feedback explaining the wrong guess, without requiring a new test or treating the correction as a leaked answer.
